lenses.name: missing canonical guard
lenses.question: Can the operation reach a privileged sink without the intended canonical control?
evidence_requirements: The canonical guard definition and the invariant it is intended to enforce.
Control-flow evidence for every path that can reach the protected sink.
false_positive_traps: A guard missing on one function is not a bypass if every reachable caller enforces the same invariant canonically.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Compare path traces statically; if authorized, use an owned denied-case fixture against the canonical and suspected alternate path.

lenses.name: null or missing identity
lenses.question: Does a missing identity, owner, tenant, actor or subject fail closed?
evidence_requirements: Identity/tenant/owner type definitions, including nullable or anonymous states.
Evidence of the effective decision made when identity resolution returns no subject.
false_positive_traps: An anonymous path may be intentionally public; absence matters only when a protected decision consumes it.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use a synthetic anonymous identity and an owned protected object; do not use another person's account or data.

lenses.name: lookup/read error
lenses.question: If a security-relevant lookup errors, does the path refuse rather than continue with a safe-looking default?
evidence_requirements: The error branches of each security-relevant lookup and their returned decision.
A bounded failure observation or test double showing the downstream path on lookup error.
false_positive_traps: A theoretically permissive branch is not reachable evidence if the lookup implementation cannot return that error state.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Prefer a local stub that returns a controlled error and assert that the operation refuses without external side effects.

lenses.name: alternate endpoint
lenses.question: Does a sibling route, RPC, bulk path, search path or background worker bypass the primary control?
evidence_requirements: A route/RPC/worker inventory grouped by shared privileged sink or invariant.
Guard traces for the primary path and every sibling or asynchronous path.
false_positive_traps: Similar route names do not prove equivalent authority or access to the same protected object.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise only owned fixtures through alternate paths after static sink matching; keep provider calls mocked.

lenses.name: direct-object access
lenses.question: Can a caller skip UI/navigation and act directly on an object they should not control?
evidence_requirements: The server-side object ownership or tenancy model and canonical authorization decision.
A two-identity trace showing how direct object identifiers are resolved and checked.
false_positive_traps: Predictable or visible object identifiers alone are not an authorization failure.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use two synthetic identities and their own objects; attempt only a reversible cross-fixture read or no-op mutation.

lenses.name: bulk operation
lenses.question: Does the bulk path enforce the same per-object invariants and report partial results honestly?
evidence_requirements: Per-item authorization/invariant enforcement inside the bulk implementation.
Transaction and partial-result behavior for a mixed-validity batch.
false_positive_traps: Whole-batch rejection does not by itself demonstrate that every item received the intended check.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use a tiny batch of owned synthetic objects with one deliberately invalid item and no real external effects.

lenses.name: search/export/list
lenses.question: Can listing, search, export or autocomplete reveal objects more broadly than item endpoints allow?
evidence_requirements: Query scoping, pagination, field selection, and response filtering for list/search/export paths.
Role-separated observations over a synthetic corpus with known visibility.
false_positive_traps: Hiding an item in the UI is not evidence that the server list endpoint enforces visibility.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Populate a minimal synthetic corpus for two test roles and compare identifiers and fields, not real customer records.

lenses.name: client/server trust
lenses.question: Does client-provided state overrule stored/server/provider truth?
evidence_requirements: A source-of-truth map for every security- or value-relevant field.
The server/provider validation trace from client input to durable or external decision.
false_positive_traps: Client-controlled fields are not a defect when the server independently derives or verifies the authoritative value.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Tamper only synthetic fixture values and assert server-side recomputation with provider integrations stubbed.

lenses.name: stale state
lenses.question: Can a stale preview, token, assignment, cache, price or object state be replayed after reality changed?
evidence_requirements: Version, expiry, cache invalidation, or compare-and-set controls for mutable security state.
A timeline showing the observed decision before and after the underlying state changes.
false_positive_traps: The existence of a cache or preview is not evidence that stale data remains authoritative at commit time.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Change an owned fixture between preview and commit, then assert rejection or safe recomputation.

lenses.name: retry/replay
lenses.question: Can retry or replay duplicate an external or internal side effect?
evidence_requirements: Idempotency keys, uniqueness constraints, provider identifiers, and replay-window behavior.
A repeated-request trace that correlates internal and external effects.
false_positive_traps: Repeating a read-only or explicitly repeatable operation does not establish duplicate side effects.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Replay one identical local-fixture request with a mocked provider and count durable effects.

lenses.name: concurrency
lenses.question: Can two legitimate requests interleave into an invalid state or double effect?
evidence_requirements: Locking, isolation, compare-and-set, or uniqueness controls protecting the shared invariant.
A synchronized trace demonstrating the possible interleaving and final durable state.
false_positive_traps: Two concurrent code paths are not a race finding without a shared invariant and feasible overlap.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use deterministic barriers in a disposable local store; avoid load against shared or production systems.

lenses.name: process crash
lenses.question: What happens if the process dies between external side effect and durable commit?
evidence_requirements: Durable state boundaries around external effects, including outbox/inbox or recovery markers.
Restart/reconciliation behavior for each crash point between effect and commit.
false_positive_traps: An ordinary caught exception is not equivalent to process termination and restart.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Fault-inject only in a controlled fixture with fake providers, then restart and reconcile from durable state.

lenses.name: timeout/outcome unknown
lenses.question: Is a timeout distinguished from definitive failure so late success cannot be duplicated?
evidence_requirements: Timeout classification, provider operation identifiers, and reconciliation logic.
A late-success trace showing whether retry can distinguish unknown outcome from definitive failure.
false_positive_traps: A timeout alone does not prove failure or duplication; the eventual provider outcome must be correlated.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use a provider stub that completes after the caller times out and assert one reconciled effect.

lenses.name: partial success
lenses.question: Can partial fulfillment, write, payment or mutation be represented as full success?
evidence_requirements: Transaction/compensation boundaries for multi-step operations.
Response and persisted state when one controlled sub-operation fails.
false_positive_traps: An intermediate partial write is not externally observable partial success if guaranteed compensation completes before response.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Fail one step in an owned multi-item fixture and verify both the returned status and final durable state.

lenses.name: terminal-state transition
lenses.question: Can a supposedly terminal state be reopened, reclaimed, refunded or mutated incorrectly?
evidence_requirements: The authoritative transition table, including terminal states and privileged overrides.
Enforcement evidence at every mutation path that can change the state.
false_positive_traps: A documented administrative recovery transition is not an unauthorized reopening.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Attempt invalid transitions on synthetic state-machine records and assert no external side effect.

lenses.name: default/coercion
lenses.question: Can null, NaN, empty, false or unknown be coerced into zero/free/allowed/healthy?
evidence_requirements: Parsing, validation, defaulting, and coercion sites for the relevant value.
Boundary-case observations for null, empty, non-finite, false, zero, and unknown values as applicable.
false_positive_traps: A language coercion quirk is not relevant when the coerced value never reaches a security or integrity decision.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use typed local fixtures for boundary values and assert explicit refusal or intentional defaults.

lenses.name: normalization mismatch
lenses.question: Can equivalent inputs bypass validation because different layers normalize differently?
evidence_requirements: Normalization/canonicalization rules at each parser, service, store, and provider boundary.
Equivalent-input comparisons showing the value used for validation and the value used at the sink.
false_positive_traps: Cosmetic representation differences are not bypasses when every layer compares the same canonical value.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Test a small equivalence set of inert strings locally; never use destructive payloads.

lenses.name: stored/second-order input
lenses.question: Can previously stored attacker-controlled data become dangerous when reused in a later query, command, render or tool call?
evidence_requirements: Input provenance from initial storage through every later query, render, command, or tool-call sink.
The escaping, parameterization, or allowlisting effective at the later-use context.
false_positive_traps: Storing untrusted text is not a defect unless a later context interprets it unsafely.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Trace an inert sentinel through the full lifecycle; avoid live exploit strings and external commands.

lenses.name: boundary mismatch
lenses.question: Do UI, API, database, worker and provider layers disagree about the same invariant?
evidence_requirements: The same invariant stated for UI, API, worker, database, and provider layers that participate.
A cross-layer trace identifying which layer owns the final decision.
false_positive_traps: Different implementations are not inconsistent when a downstream canonical layer still enforces the invariant.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use contract fixtures at adjacent boundaries and compare decisions without invoking real providers.

lenses.name: secret/PII exposure
lenses.question: Can responses, logs, bundles, traces, analytics or errors expose secrets or sensitive customer data?
evidence_requirements: A sensitive-data inventory mapped to response, log, trace, analytics, bundle, and error sinks.
Redacted artifact samples proving the fields actually emitted and accessible to each audience.
false_positive_traps: A sensitive-looking variable name is not exposure evidence without a reachable output and unauthorized audience.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use synthetic canary values, never real secrets or PII, and preserve redacted proof only.

lenses.name: configuration drift
lenses.question: Does an absent, shadow, legacy or environment-specific flag silently disable the intended control?
evidence_requirements: Configuration schema, defaults, environment overlays, and deployment manifests.
Effective configuration evidence for supported environments, including absent and legacy keys.
false_positive_traps: An environment difference may be intentional and safe when validated by a fail-closed startup policy.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise missing, shadow, and legacy flags in a local process or config parser; do not mutate shared environments.

lenses.name: migration/version drift
lenses.question: Can repo history differ from live schema/function truth in a way that makes deployment unsafe?
evidence_requirements: Ordered migration history and the expected schema/function version contract.
A live or disposable schema snapshot compared with repository truth and deployment ordering.
false_positive_traps: An unapplied migration in a development database is not release drift unless that environment is expected to be current.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Run upgrade/rollback checks only on disposable databases populated with synthetic state.

lenses.name: supply-chain substitution
lenses.question: Can an untrusted package/action/artifact/source be substituted for the intended dependency?
evidence_requirements: Lockfiles, resolved sources, signatures/attestations, and allowed publisher or action policy.
Build evidence showing the exact dependency or artifact selected from the declared source.
false_positive_traps: A vulnerable dependency alert is not evidence of package substitution or provenance failure.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use offline fixture manifests and verification commands; never publish test packages or alter a public namespace.

lenses.name: browser/runtime-only failure
lenses.question: Can bundling, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration or runtime behavior invalidate a control despite green type/unit tests?
evidence_requirements: Built-asset, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration, and runtime header evidence from the relevant environment.
A browser/runtime trace connecting the observed behavior to the intended security control.
false_positive_traps: A unit-test mismatch or console error is not a security failure without impact on the control.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use a local browser fixture or authorized staging account with inert data and reduced side effects.

lenses.name: agent/tool confusion
lenses.question: Can untrusted content influence tool choice, target, authority, or claimed operator identity?
evidence_requirements: Tool schemas, authority policy, context provenance, and operator/agent identity binding.
A trace from untrusted content through model decision to the proposed or executed tool call.
false_positive_traps: Model-generated text is not a tool-authorization failure when no privileged call is possible or executed.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Use fake tools and synthetic instructions; require confirmation and block real external actions.

lenses.name: observability honesty
lenses.question: Can success, health, status, audit or metrics claim an invariant that was not actually proven?
evidence_requirements: The actual operation outcome and the code that emits status, health, audit, or metrics.
Correlated failure/success evidence showing whether observable claims match durable reality.
false_positive_traps: A missing log is not the same as a false success claim; identify the consumer and asserted invariant.
lenses.safe_test_guidance: Simulate a controlled local failure and assert returned status plus audit/metric output without exporting telemetry.

evidence_requirements: Transaction/compensation boundaries for multi-step operations.
Response and persisted state when one controlled sub-operation fails.
false_positive_traps: An intermediate partial write is not externally observable partial success if guaranteed compensation completes before response.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Fail one step in an owned multi-item fixture and verify both the returned status and final durable state.

hypotheses.title: API Security — terminal-state transition
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the terminal-state transition condition. Question to resolve: Can a supposedly terminal state be reopened, reclaimed, refunded or mutated incorrectly?
evidence_requirements: The authoritative transition table, including terminal states and privileged overrides.
Enforcement evidence at every mutation path that can change the state.
false_positive_traps: A documented administrative recovery transition is not an unauthorized reopening.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Attempt invalid transitions on synthetic state-machine records and assert no external side effect.

hypotheses.title: API Security — default/coercion
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the default/coercion condition. Question to resolve: Can null, NaN, empty, false or unknown be coerced into zero/free/allowed/healthy?
evidence_requirements: Parsing, validation, defaulting, and coercion sites for the relevant value.
Boundary-case observations for null, empty, non-finite, false, zero, and unknown values as applicable.
false_positive_traps: A language coercion quirk is not relevant when the coerced value never reaches a security or integrity decision.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use typed local fixtures for boundary values and assert explicit refusal or intentional defaults.

hypotheses.title: API Security — normalization mismatch
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the normalization mismatch condition. Question to resolve: Can equivalent inputs bypass validation because different layers normalize differently?
evidence_requirements: Normalization/canonicalization rules at each parser, service, store, and provider boundary.
Equivalent-input comparisons showing the value used for validation and the value used at the sink.
false_positive_traps: Cosmetic representation differences are not bypasses when every layer compares the same canonical value.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Test a small equivalence set of inert strings locally; never use destructive payloads.

hypotheses.title: API Security — stored/second-order input
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the stored/second-order input condition. Question to resolve: Can previously stored attacker-controlled data become dangerous when reused in a later query, command, render or tool call?
evidence_requirements: Input provenance from initial storage through every later query, render, command, or tool-call sink.
The escaping, parameterization, or allowlisting effective at the later-use context.
false_positive_traps: Storing untrusted text is not a defect unless a later context interprets it unsafely.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Trace an inert sentinel through the full lifecycle; avoid live exploit strings and external commands.

hypotheses.title: API Security — boundary mismatch
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the boundary mismatch condition. Question to resolve: Do UI, API, database, worker and provider layers disagree about the same invariant?
evidence_requirements: The same invariant stated for UI, API, worker, database, and provider layers that participate.
A cross-layer trace identifying which layer owns the final decision.
false_positive_traps: Different implementations are not inconsistent when a downstream canonical layer still enforces the invariant.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use contract fixtures at adjacent boundaries and compare decisions without invoking real providers.

hypotheses.title: API Security — secret/PII exposure
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the secret/PII exposure condition. Question to resolve: Can responses, logs, bundles, traces, analytics or errors expose secrets or sensitive customer data?
evidence_requirements: A sensitive-data inventory mapped to response, log, trace, analytics, bundle, and error sinks.
Redacted artifact samples proving the fields actually emitted and accessible to each audience.
false_positive_traps: A sensitive-looking variable name is not exposure evidence without a reachable output and unauthorized audience.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use synthetic canary values, never real secrets or PII, and preserve redacted proof only.

hypotheses.title: API Security — configuration drift
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the configuration drift condition. Question to resolve: Does an absent, shadow, legacy or environment-specific flag silently disable the intended control?
evidence_requirements: Configuration schema, defaults, environment overlays, and deployment manifests.
Effective configuration evidence for supported environments, including absent and legacy keys.
false_positive_traps: An environment difference may be intentional and safe when validated by a fail-closed startup policy.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise missing, shadow, and legacy flags in a local process or config parser; do not mutate shared environments.

hypotheses.title: API Security — migration/version drift
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the migration/version drift condition. Question to resolve: Can repo history differ from live schema/function truth in a way that makes deployment unsafe?
evidence_requirements: Ordered migration history and the expected schema/function version contract.
A live or disposable schema snapshot compared with repository truth and deployment ordering.
false_positive_traps: An unapplied migration in a development database is not release drift unless that environment is expected to be current.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Run upgrade/rollback checks only on disposable databases populated with synthetic state.

hypotheses.title: API Security — supply-chain substitution
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the supply-chain substitution condition. Question to resolve: Can an untrusted package/action/artifact/source be substituted for the intended dependency?
evidence_requirements: Lockfiles, resolved sources, signatures/attestations, and allowed publisher or action policy.

false_positive_traps: A vulnerable dependency alert is not evidence of package substitution or provenance failure.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use offline fixture manifests and verification commands; never publish test packages or alter a public namespace.

hypotheses.title: API Security — browser/runtime-only failure
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the browser/runtime-only failure condition. Question to resolve: Can bundling, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration or runtime behavior invalidate a control despite green type/unit tests?
evidence_requirements: Built-asset, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration, and runtime header evidence from the relevant environment.
A browser/runtime trace connecting the observed behavior to the intended security control.
false_positive_traps: A unit-test mismatch or console error is not a security failure without impact on the control.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use a local browser fixture or authorized staging account with inert data and reduced side effects.

hypotheses.title: API Security — agent/tool confusion
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the agent/tool confusion condition. Question to resolve: Can untrusted content influence tool choice, target, authority, or claimed operator identity?
evidence_requirements: Tool schemas, authority policy, context provenance, and operator/agent identity binding.

false_positive_traps: Model-generated text is not a tool-authorization failure when no privileged call is possible or executed.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use fake tools and synthetic instructions; require confirmation and block real external actions.

hypotheses.title: API Security — observability honesty
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether schema, mass assignment, pagination, filters, webhooks, RPC and error behavior exhibits the observability honesty condition. Question to resolve: Can success, health, status, audit or metrics claim an invariant that was not actually proven?

false_positive_traps: A missing log is not the same as a false success claim; identify the consumer and asserted invariant.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Simulate a controlled local failure and assert returned status plus audit/metric output without exporting telemetry.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — missing canonical guard
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the missing canonical guard condition. Question to resolve: Can the operation reach a privileged sink without the intended canonical control?

false_positive_traps: A guard missing on one function is not a bypass if every reachable caller enforces the same invariant canonically.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Compare path traces statically; if authorized, use an owned denied-case fixture against the canonical and suspected alternate path.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — null or missing identity
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the null or missing identity condition. Question to resolve: Does a missing identity, owner, tenant, actor or subject fail closed?
evidence_requirements: Identity/tenant/owner type definitions, including nullable or anonymous states.

false_positive_traps: An anonymous path may be intentionally public; absence matters only when a protected decision consumes it.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — lookup/read error
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the lookup/read error condition. Question to resolve: If a security-relevant lookup errors, does the path refuse rather than continue with a safe-looking default?

false_positive_traps: A theoretically permissive branch is not reachable evidence if the lookup implementation cannot return that error state.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — alternate endpoint
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the alternate endpoint condition. Question to resolve: Does a sibling route, RPC, bulk path, search path or background worker bypass the primary control?
evidence_requirements: A route/RPC/worker inventory grouped by shared privileged sink or invariant.

false_positive_traps: Similar route names do not prove equivalent authority or access to the same protected object.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise only owned fixtures through alternate paths after static sink matching; keep provider calls mocked.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — direct-object access
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the direct-object access condition. Question to resolve: Can a caller skip UI/navigation and act directly on an object they should not control?

false_positive_traps: Predictable or visible object identifiers alone are not an authorization failure.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — bulk operation

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — search/export/list

hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the client/server trust condition. Question to resolve: Does client-provided state overrule stored/server/provider truth?

false_positive_traps: Client-controlled fields are not a defect when the server independently derives or verifies the authoritative value.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — stale state

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — retry/replay

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — concurrency
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether type confusion, path traversal, archives, parsers, storage and serving exhibits the concurrency condition. Question to resolve: Can two legitimate requests interleave into an invalid state or double effect?

false_positive_traps: Two concurrent code paths are not a race finding without a shared invariant and feasible overlap.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use deterministic barriers in a disposable local store; avoid load against shared or production systems.

hypotheses.title: Files / Uploads — process crash

false_positive_traps: An ordinary caught exception is not equivalent to process termination and restart.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Fault-inject only in a controlled fixture with fake providers, then restart and reconcile from durable state.

Question to resolve: Can bundling, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration or runtime behavior invalidate a control despite green type/unit tests?
evidence_requirements: Built-asset, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration, and runtime header evidence from the relevant environment.
A browser/runtime trace connecting the observed behavior to the intended security control.
false_positive_traps: A unit-test mismatch or console error is not a security failure without impact on the control.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use a local browser fixture or authorized staging account with inert data and reduced side effects.

hypotheses.title: Operational Security — agent/tool confusion
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether admin tooling, support workflows, break-glass, monitoring, runbooks and incident paths exhibits the agent/tool confusion condition. Question to resolve: Can untrusted content influence tool choice, target, authority, or claimed operator identity?
evidence_requirements: Tool schemas, authority policy, context provenance, and operator/agent identity binding.
A trace from untrusted content through model decision to the proposed or executed tool call.
false_positive_traps: Model-generated text is not a tool-authorization failure when no privileged call is possible or executed.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use fake tools and synthetic instructions; require confirmation and block real external actions.

hypotheses.title: Operational Security — observability honesty
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether admin tooling, support workflows, break-glass, monitoring, runbooks and incident paths exhibits the observability honesty condition. Question to resolve: Can success, health, status, audit or metrics claim an invariant that was not actually proven?

Correlated failure/success evidence showing whether observable claims match durable reality.
false_positive_traps: A missing log is not the same as a false success claim; identify the consumer and asserted invariant.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Simulate a controlled local failure and assert returned status plus audit/metric output without exporting telemetry.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — missing canonical guard
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the missing canonical guard condition. Question to resolve: Can the operation reach a privileged sink without the intended canonical control?

Control-flow evidence for every path that can reach the protected sink.
false_positive_traps: A guard missing on one function is not a bypass if every reachable caller enforces the same invariant canonically.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Compare path traces statically; if authorized, use an owned denied-case fixture against the canonical and suspected alternate path.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — null or missing identity
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the null or missing identity condition. Question to resolve: Does a missing identity, owner, tenant, actor or subject fail closed?
evidence_requirements: Identity/tenant/owner type definitions, including nullable or anonymous states.

false_positive_traps: An anonymous path may be intentionally public; absence matters only when a protected decision consumes it.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use a synthetic anonymous identity and an owned protected object; do not use another person's account or data.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — lookup/read error
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the lookup/read error condition. Question to resolve: If a security-relevant lookup errors, does the path refuse rather than continue with a safe-looking default?

false_positive_traps: A theoretically permissive branch is not reachable evidence if the lookup implementation cannot return that error state.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Prefer a local stub that returns a controlled error and assert that the operation refuses without external side effects.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — alternate endpoint
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the alternate endpoint condition. Question to resolve: Does a sibling route, RPC, bulk path, search path or background worker bypass the primary control?

false_positive_traps: Similar route names do not prove equivalent authority or access to the same protected object.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise only owned fixtures through alternate paths after static sink matching; keep provider calls mocked.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — direct-object access

false_positive_traps: Predictable or visible object identifiers alone are not an authorization failure.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — bulk operation

hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use a tiny batch of owned synthetic objects with one deliberately invalid item and no real external effects.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — search/export/list
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the search/export/list condition. Question to resolve: Can listing, search, export or autocomplete reveal objects more broadly than item endpoints allow?

false_positive_traps: Hiding an item in the UI is not evidence that the server list endpoint enforces visibility.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — client/server trust

hypotheses.title: Release Security — stale state
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the stale state condition. Question to resolve: Can a stale preview, token, assignment, cache, price or object state be replayed after reality changed?

hypotheses.title: Release Security — retry/replay

hypotheses.title: Release Security — concurrency
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether build truth, migration gates, feature flags, rollback, smoke and post-deploy observation exhibits the concurrency condition. Question to resolve: Can two legitimate requests interleave into an invalid state or double effect?

false_positive_traps: Two concurrent code paths are not a race finding without a shared invariant and feasible overlap.

hypotheses.title: Release Security — process crash

hypotheses.title: Release Security — timeout/outcome unknown

hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the boundary mismatch condition. Question to resolve: Do UI, API, database, worker and provider layers disagree about the same invariant?
evidence_requirements: The same invariant stated for UI, API, worker, database, and provider layers that participate.
A cross-layer trace identifying which layer owns the final decision.
false_positive_traps: Different implementations are not inconsistent when a downstream canonical layer still enforces the invariant.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use contract fixtures at adjacent boundaries and compare decisions without invoking real providers.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — secret/PII exposure
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the secret/PII exposure condition. Question to resolve: Can responses, logs, bundles, traces, analytics or errors expose secrets or sensitive customer data?
evidence_requirements: A sensitive-data inventory mapped to response, log, trace, analytics, bundle, and error sinks.
Redacted artifact samples proving the fields actually emitted and accessible to each audience.
false_positive_traps: A sensitive-looking variable name is not exposure evidence without a reachable output and unauthorized audience.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use synthetic canary values, never real secrets or PII, and preserve redacted proof only.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — configuration drift
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the configuration drift condition. Question to resolve: Does an absent, shadow, legacy or environment-specific flag silently disable the intended control?
evidence_requirements: Configuration schema, defaults, environment overlays, and deployment manifests.
Effective configuration evidence for supported environments, including absent and legacy keys.
false_positive_traps: An environment difference may be intentional and safe when validated by a fail-closed startup policy.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Exercise missing, shadow, and legacy flags in a local process or config parser; do not mutate shared environments.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — migration/version drift
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the migration/version drift condition. Question to resolve: Can repo history differ from live schema/function truth in a way that makes deployment unsafe?
evidence_requirements: Ordered migration history and the expected schema/function version contract.
A live or disposable schema snapshot compared with repository truth and deployment ordering.
false_positive_traps: An unapplied migration in a development database is not release drift unless that environment is expected to be current.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Run upgrade/rollback checks only on disposable databases populated with synthetic state.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — supply-chain substitution
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the supply-chain substitution condition. Question to resolve: Can an untrusted package/action/artifact/source be substituted for the intended dependency?
evidence_requirements: Lockfiles, resolved sources, signatures/attestations, and allowed publisher or action policy.
Build evidence showing the exact dependency or artifact selected from the declared source.
false_positive_traps: A vulnerable dependency alert is not evidence of package substitution or provenance failure.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use offline fixture manifests and verification commands; never publish test packages or alter a public namespace.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — browser/runtime-only failure
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the browser/runtime-only failure condition. Question to resolve: Can bundling, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration or runtime behavior invalidate a control despite green type/unit tests?
evidence_requirements: Built-asset, origin, cookie, CSP, hydration, and runtime header evidence from the relevant environment.
A browser/runtime trace connecting the observed behavior to the intended security control.
false_positive_traps: A unit-test mismatch or console error is not a security failure without impact on the control.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use a local browser fixture or authorized staging account with inert data and reduced side effects.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — agent/tool confusion
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the agent/tool confusion condition. Question to resolve: Can untrusted content influence tool choice, target, authority, or claimed operator identity?
evidence_requirements: Tool schemas, authority policy, context provenance, and operator/agent identity binding.
A trace from untrusted content through model decision to the proposed or executed tool call.
false_positive_traps: Model-generated text is not a tool-authorization failure when no privileged call is possible or executed.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Use fake tools and synthetic instructions; require confirmation and block real external actions.

hypotheses.title: Attack Surface Mapping — observability honesty
hypotheses.hypothesis: Review whether entrypoints, identities, assets, trust boundaries, external integrations and state machines exhibits the observability honesty condition. Question to resolve: Can success, health, status, audit or metrics claim an invariant that was not actually proven?
evidence_requirements: The actual operation outcome and the code that emits status, health, audit, or metrics.
Correlated failure/success evidence showing whether observable claims match durable reality.
false_positive_traps: A missing log is not the same as a false success claim; identify the consumer and asserted invariant.
hypotheses.safe_test_guidance: Simulate a controlled local failure and assert returned status plus audit/metric output without exporting telemetry.

selection_rule: Evaluate every record with the deterministic four-state applicability engine before review; missing evidence is UNKNOWN and only explicit absence is NOT_APPLICABLE.
claim_policy: Every catalog record is an unverified hypothesis. Findings require an evidence chain and, for High/Critical, independent verification.
